config.classes_note: Three classes, each sourced from the field by locus and matching the census's own lineage ('scholarly record'), kind ('publication model and service ecosystem') and provenance_object ('an assertion'): FAIR data containers (B1 home headline; B6 Abstract; B8); provenance for individual assertions (B1 home, the Provenance part; B6 Abstract; the IEEE card's title); machine-readable scientific publishing, the claim-level decomposition of the scholarly record (B4 snippet; B8; B7). The aliases are the entity's name in its forms (nanopublication(s), nanopub(s)), its domains, its software (nanopub-py, nanopub-java, nanopub-http, nanopub-server, Nanodash, Nanopub Registry, Query and Monitor), Knowledge Pixels (named by B7 as the company behind nanopub.net and Nanodash), Trusty URIs (B6: the identifiers that make nanopublications permanent) and the founding citation 'Mons and Velterop'. 'Knowledge Pixels' and 'Trusty URI' are admitted at D only where the sentence or paragraph bears on nanopublications. Admission by reading (§3.4): a candidate is admitted when its sentence or paragraph makes a claim bearing on nanopublications (what they are, what they carry, what they leave out, where they stand among the archive's instruments or the archive's own adoption of their practice); a reference-list entry or a bare listing is not a claim. O-class admits a sentence that applies an archive category (provenance erasure, the Provenance Erasure Rate, the training layer against the composition layer, the Claim Status Packet, training-layer literature) to a sourced class as a class.
